subject: 🤖 Axios PM: Anthropic IPO on course

Axios PM
By Mike Allen · Sep 14, 2026

☕️ Good Monday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 654 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

⚡️ Situational awareness: President Trump lashed out on Truth Social at calls for new AI guardrails and protections, arguing AI only needs a "STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT" and that AI critics should "BEWARE!" Go deeper.
 
 
1 big thing: Anthropic IPO still on schedule
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios

Anthropic is still likely to go public this year, even as AI safety rockets into the zeitgeist, multiple sources tell Axios' Dan Primack.

There have been whispers that Anthropic might want to wait, due to new product liability and regulation questions.

  • Yet the Claude maker might actually view the focus on AI risks as elevating the case for its IPO rather than dampening it, arguing that safety is improved via the transparency of being a public company.
  • OpenAI, meanwhile, was leaning toward a 2027 listing — and still seems to be doing so.

🖼️ The big picture: Anthropic's business, and investor FOMO, are unchanged from last week.

  • Yes, Anthropic has pledged to have third-party evaluation of its models, and suggested some pacing that might slow new model releases.
  • But so did its top rival — and there's still an insane amount of untapped revenue tied to existing models.

🤖 It's also not like Anthropic would be the first or only listed frontier AI lab, as Alphabet and SpaceX shares continue to trade.

  • There's also a cynical argument that "pacing" could reduce Anthropic's compute spend, thus improving its financials.

Some accuse the company of pursuing a policy of regulatory capture — and if you buy that argument, you'll probably also buy Anthropic stock.

  • Finally, it still needs the money. It could delay and raise more via private markets, but no frontier lab can just sit on the capital markets sidelines.

Go deeper.
 
 
2. 📚 Most-borrowed books
 
Data: OverDrive/Libby. Chart: Sami Sparber/Axios

"The Calamity Club" was last month's most-borrowed e-book on Libby, Axios' Sami Sparber reports.

  • Author Kathryn Stockett's bestseller explores poverty and friendship through the eyes of two outcast women in 1930s Mississippi.

🍿 The big picture: Libby's top 20 features several "BookTok" favorites that have already been adapted for the screen, or are slated to be.

  • That includes "Yesteryear" by Caro Claire Burke (a thriller about a tradwife influencer that Anne Hathaway is set to star in and produce) and "The Deal" by Elle Kennedy (the basis for Amazon Prime Video's hit hockey romance series "Off Campus.")

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
A tarp covers the lettering on the facade of the Kennedy Center in June. Photo: Valerie Plesch/Bloomberg via Getty Images
  1. 🎻 The Kennedy Center Board of Trustees is planning to propose adding President Trump's name to the facility's exterior in recognition of his saving the building from its "precarious fiscal position," per a new court filing. Go deeper.
  2. 🏭 The EPA is repealing rules that limit planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions from power plants fueled by coal and natural gas. Go deeper.
  3. ❄️ Weather traders are betting that a potentially historic El Niño will translate into a relatively mild winter, Bloomberg reports. Gift link.
  4. 🎤 Macklemore was dropped from Ed Sheeran's U.S. tour after saying "Free Palestine" and performing a protest song alongside images of Gaza during a Sept. 4 show at MetLife Stadium. He wrote on Instagram today: "If those words cost me the stage, while turning the conversation back to Palestine, then it was the most successful tour I've ever been on." Go deeper.
 
 
4. 🍭 1 for the road: It's texture time
 
Nerds Gummy Clusters. Photo: Lane Turner/The Boston Globe via Getty Images

Texture is having a crunchy, gooey moment in the food and beverage world.

  • For many people, the way a menu item or packaged snack feels in the mouth has become as big a draw as flavor, AP reports.

🍫 The importance of "mouthfeel," a food science term for oral sensation, has inspired new products like Starbucks' Aerocano (an air-whipped iced espresso), Power Crunch (a wafer-like protein bar) and Trolli Gummi Popz (which are frozen but still soft and chewy).

  • Puratos, a Belgian company that develops commercial-grade ingredients for chocolate and baked goods, tells AP that texture "has evolved from a complementary feature to a defining aspect of food quality."
